new: Decision for you. Lisa's only sample is Zilber's certificate for Riley (GC on the Janesville shell building). It is higher than Pinnacle's form on every line: general aggregate $2M (manual $1M), products-completed operations $2M ($1M), auto $2M ($1M), umbrella $10M ($5M), plus employers' liability $1M. Matching it would raise the limits, not lower them.
Options: (a) keep the manual's limits, umbrella $5M; (b) match Zilber's sample; (c) ask Lisa whether a lower standard exists for site work.

Whichever you pick, fix the wording. The manual names the Owner and the Village as additional insured under (i), (ii) and (iii), but (i) is workers' compensation. The sample puts additional insured on general liability only (endorsements CG 2038 and CG 2037) and waives subrogation on general liability and workers' comp. Keep the Village, which the sample does not name. The manual asks for 30 days' written notice of cancellation; the sample only says notice per policy provisions.
B4.why: You asked to see Zilber's insurance first (11/4). Lisa's sample is a Riley certificate, not a utility-contractor standard, and she did not say it applies to site work. The Village as additional insured stays either way (DA approval letter, condition 6c).

new: Use Zilber's form. Partial with each progress payment (unconditional for amounts already paid, conditional for the current draw) and Final with the last payment.
